character_facts: Janus-Jana is shown as an imperial ruler in elaborate ceremonial or military regalia.
Aghnar is portrayed in the recap as powerful, feared, aging, and available for hire as a mercenary.
Aghnar is said to be capable of defeating all existing imperial solutions.
Steelhead is described as faceless or featureless and capable of extreme psychic or spiritual force.
Oda/Honoratza is associated with the reveal behind the Techno-Techno ambassador projection.
continuity_links: This page functions as a 'previously in The Metabarons' summary connecting earlier imperial, mercenary, and Pthagurean plotlines to the coming duel.
It directly sets up the confrontation between Steelhead and the Metabaron as the next major conflict.
dialogue_meaning: The prose explains that Aghnar publicly breaks with the Empire and stops serving it.
It states that Aghnar later accepts a genocidal contract from the Pthagureans against the Empire.
It explains that the Empire cannot find a conventional way to defeat the Metabaron.
It reveals that the supposed Techno-Techno envoy is a disguise leading to the presentation of Steelhead as a counterforce.
It sets up an imminent duel between Steelhead and the Metabaron, with both sides massing spacecraft.
lore_facts: Janus-Jana is identified as Emperoress and is associated with the Imperial Palace.
Aghnar is referred to as the new Metabaron in the recap.
Aghnar once served the Empire but later renounced that service.
Anasirma is identified as Aghnar's natal planet, described here as reduced to its last remains.
The Pthagureans seek control of the galaxy and are willing to exterminate all life in the Empire to achieve it.
The Techno-Techno can project or employ holo-images.
Steelhead pilots or is associated with a purple Metacraft.
The Metabaron pilots or is associated with a black Metacraft.
plot_events: The page recaps earlier story events rather than depicting a new scene.
At the Imperial Palace, Janus-Jana oversees the arming of Purple Endoguards when Aghnar enters, kills guards, and announces he is ending his service to the Empire.
Aghnar becomes a mercenary and sells his services to many clients over a span of years.
In a secret lair on Anasirma, Aghnar notices his own aging while looking in a mirror.
A delegation of Pthagureans offers Aghnar payment to exterminate all life within the Empire so they can seize the galaxy, and he accepts.
Panic spreads in the Imperial Palace because no weapon can defeat the Metabaron.
A Techno-Techno ambassador appears as a holo-image, then reveals Oda/Honoratza and Aghnar's son Steelhead.
Steelhead demonstrates overwhelming power by reshaping the Imperial dome into a gigantic golden flower.
Steelhead is chosen as humanity's champion and a duel is arranged between him and the Metabaron, with fleets gathering around their respective Metacraft.
uncertainties: Several proper names are difficult to read precisely from the image; spellings such as 'Anasirma,' 'Pthagureans,' and 'Oda/Honoratza' may be imperfect.
The five small circular portraits at the bottom are not labeled on-page, so not every face can be identified with certainty.
Because this is a recap/credits page, most events are narrated in summary prose rather than shown directly in sequential panels.
visual_summary: A recap and credits page for The Metabarons. The page is dominated by a large painted portrait of Empress Janus-Jana in ornate armor and jewelry, with a decorative sci-fi border and five small circular character portraits along the bottom. The right side contains a prose summary of prior events, and the bottom band contains creator and publication credits.
